purpose: Test whether a smaller start ritual reduces delay on a chosen writing project.
boundaries: Do not retain raw journal text

preferences.statement: The user prefers direct recommendations after a short context check.

evidence.statement: The user reports starting more easily when the next paragraph is named.
evidence.context: The selected writing project during the current work period.

evidence.statement: Energy and competing workload have not yet been compared.
evidence.context: The selected writing project during the current work period.

goals.statement: Start the selected writing task on three planned weekdays.
goals.success_evidence: A timestamped five-minute start on three planned days.
goals.stop_condition: Pause if the plan displaces required sleep.

hypotheses.statement: The first-step ambiguity may contribute more to delay than lack of interest.
hypotheses.context_boundary: Only this writing project during the current work period.

hypotheses.statement: The planned time may conflict with the user's available energy.
hypotheses.context_boundary: Only this writing project during the current work period.

experiments.question: Does naming the next five-minute action the night before reduce start delay?
experiments.action: On three planned nights, write one five-minute starting instruction for the next morning.
experiments.trigger: After closing the writing document for the day.
experiments.coping_response: If the instruction feels too large, reduce it to opening the file and adding one sentence.
experiments.evidence: Whether a five-minute start occurs and approximate delay after the planned start time.
experiments.stop_condition: Stop if it causes sleep loss or work-policy conflict.

scales.construct: Confidence in completing the five-minute start
scales.low_anchor: I do not expect to start even with the instruction.
scales.high_anchor: I expect to complete the five-minute start at the planned time.
scales.purpose: Decide whether the experiment should be made smaller before trying it.
scales.decision_link: Choose the minimum viable starting ritual.
scales.context_boundary: Tomorrow morning on the selected writing project only.

check_ins.decision_link: If confidence is below 5, reduce the starting ritual before trying it.

decisions.question: Which starting ritual should be tested first?

options.label: Prepare and use a five-minute starting instruction.
options.benefit: Directly tests whether first-step ambiguity matters.
options.cost: Requires a short preparation the night before.

options.label: Schedule a start without preparing an instruction.
options.cost: Does not isolate the ambiguity hypothesis.

decisions.rationale: The user prefers the more informative low-cost test.
assumptions: A five-minute start is feasible without displacing sleep.
unknowns: Whether morning energy or workload is the stronger constraint.
